prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py incorrectly JSON-decodes string values for union-typed parameters (e.g. `str | None`), corrupting valid string inputs that happen to look like JSON (e.g. '[1,2]', 'null', '{}'). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py incorrectly JSON-decodes string values for union-typed parameters (e.g. `str | None`), corrupting valid string inputs that happen to look like JSON (e.g. '[1,2]', 'null', '{}'). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add a helper to decide when pre_parse_json should skip json.loads for a union annotation, but the scope of the skip differs. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json treats ANY union whose members are all in {str,int,float,bool,NoneType} as skip-parse — this also disables pre-parsing for `int | None`, `bool | None`, `float | None`, etc., so a client sending the JSON literal string 'null' for one of those fields would no longer be converted to Python None and would fail validation, a regression #3056 doesn't introduce since its _is_optional_str only special-cases `str | None`. Additionally, #2032 checks union args directly against a frozenset of bare types without unwrapping Annotated, so a common `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` parameter (the idiomatic way to add a description to an optional str field) would not match the frozenset and would still be pre-parsed — meaning #2032 misses fixing the bug for annotated fields, a case #3056 explicitly handles via its _unwrap_annotated helper.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add a helper to decide when pre_parse_json should skip json.loads for a union annotation, but the scope of the skip differs. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json treats ANY union whose members are all in {str,int,float,bool,NoneType} as skip-parse — this also disables pre-parsing for `int | None`, `bool | None`, `float | None`, etc., so a client sending the JSON literal string 'null' for one of those fields would no longer be converted to Python None and would fail validation, a regression #3056 doesn't introduce since its _is_optional_str only special-cases `str | None`. clusters.pick_reason: #2478 fixes pickling generically at the MCPError base class via a `_restore_mcp_error` dispatcher (using `cls.from_error_data`, with a documented special case for UrlElicitationRequiredError's `from_error`), so every current and future MCPError subclass gets working pickle support from one place. #2555 only adds a `__reduce__` override on the single UrlElicitationRequiredError subclass, which becomes redundant once the base-class fix in #2478 is in place, and would leave any other non-trivial-constructor subclass introduced later unpicklable again. #2478 also drops the `# pragma: no cover` on the `data` property, indicating it's now exercised by a round-trip pickle test, whereas #2555 only adds coverage for the one subclass's `__reduce__` path.

members.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs introduce the identical mechanism (a new `_entered` state flag on ClientSession) to guard the same lifecycle bug, so they will conflict on the same lines of session.py and only one is needed. #1849 declares `_entered` as a proper class-level type annotation (`_entered: bool`) and also updates the TracebackType import, indicating it threads the fix through the full __aenter__/__aexit__ typing contract rather than a single inline guard. #2631's visible diff only initializes `self._entered = False` ad hoc in __init__ and adds one re-entry check in __aenter__ ('Session is already running'), which covers double-entry but its own title ('fail fast when session is not started') describes the not-yet-entered case that isn't shown being handled in its diff. #1849's title and structure map directly onto the root cause (methods called before entering the context manager hang because _task_group is None), making it the more complete basis to build on; #2631 should be closed with its re-entry check folded in if not already covered.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add a helper to decide when pre_parse_json should skip json.loads for a union annotation, but the scope of the skip differs. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json treats ANY union whose members are all in {str,int,float,bool,NoneType} as skip-parse — this also disables pre-parsing for `int | None`, `bool | None`, `float | None`, etc., so a client sending the JSON literal string 'null' for one of those fields would no longer be converted to Python None and would fail validation, a regression #3056 doesn't introduce since its _is_optional_str only special-cases `str | None`. Additionally, #2032 checks union args directly against a frozenset of bare types without unwrapping Annotated, so a common `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` parameter (the idiomatic way to add a description to an optional str field) would not match the frozenset and would still be pre-parsed — meaning #2032 misses fixing the bug for annotated fields, a case #3056 explicitly handles via its _unwrap_annotated helper.

clusters.pick_reason: Fixes the actual blocking bug by default (write buffer size 1) rather than just exposing a knob that still defaults to the buggy value of 0, and ships a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the stall during progress notifications. #2215 requires every caller to know to pass write_stream_buffer_size=1 to get the fix, so it doesn't resolve the bug on its own.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both change the size of the same zero-capacity memory object stream used for write_stream in stdio_server (write_stream, write_stream_reader = create_context_streams[SessionMessage](0)). #2215 turns both read/write buffer sizes into configurable constructor args (still defaulting to 0, i.e. no behavior change unless the caller opts in). #2654 hardcodes the write_stream buffer to 1 to fix a concrete deadlock/stall where a handler's final response send blocks while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier progress notification, and adds a BlockingStdout regression test reproducing that exact stall. The two directly conflict on the same lines and address the same root cause (zero-capacity write stream causing blocking).

clusters.pick_reason: #2478 fixes pickling generically at the MCPError base class via a `_restore_mcp_error` dispatcher (using `cls.from_error_data`, with a documented special case for UrlElicitationRequiredError's `from_error`), so every current and future MCPError subclass gets working pickle support from one place. #2555 only adds a `__reduce__` override on the single UrlElicitationRequiredError subclass, which becomes redundant once the base-class fix in #2478 is in place, and would leave any other non-trivial-constructor subclass introduced later unpicklable again. #2478 also drops the `# pragma: no cover` on the `data` property, indicating it's now exercised by a round-trip pickle test, whereas #2555 only adds coverage for the one subclass's `__reduce__` path.
